changes.now: On Earth-828, in a retro-futuristic 1960s, four astronauts gained powers from a cosmic storm and became the Fantastic Four: Reed Richards, his wife Sue Storm, her brother Johnny and their friend Ben Grimm. Sue is pregnant when the Silver Surfer arrives to announce that Galactus will devour Earth. Galactus offers to spare the planet if they give him their newborn son, Franklin. They refuse. The whole world unites behind them to trap Galactus and send him away. Sue dies sending him away, and baby Franklin brings her back.
changes.proposed: On Earth-828, in a retro-futuristic 1960s, four astronauts gained powers from a cosmic storm and became the Fantastic Four: Reed Richards, his wife Sue Storm, her brother Johnny and their friend Ben Grimm. Sue is pregnant when the Silver Surfer arrives to announce that Galactus will devour Earth. Galactus offers to spare the planet if they give him their unborn son, Franklin. They refuse. The whole world unites behind them to trap Galactus and send him away. Sue dies sending him away, and baby Franklin brings her back.
changes.evidence: Galactus makes the offer on his ship while Sue is still pregnant: he senses Reed and Sue's unborn child's cosmic power, offers to spare Earth in exchange for the child and induces labor; Franklin is born only during the escape back to Earth.

changes.now: Four siblings are given powers by a dying alien, and fight crime while keeping it from their parents. On the TVA's monitors, Earth-635972 is marked terminated.
changes.proposed: Four siblings are given powers by a being from across the universe passing his on, and their parents know about them. On the TVA's monitors, Earth-635972 is marked terminated.
changes.evidence: The 1991 Power Pack TV pilot changed the comics: the children's parents are aware of their powers (their father gathers them to discuss the powers), and the pilot's story is a ghost (Dr. Mobius) haunting their new home, not crime-fighting. The powers come from an unseen entity who, after travelling the universe, decides to pass on his powers.
